opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kim Dunn (employee ID E048) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 6 note(s) about employee E048.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Kim Dunn (E048) is a full-time Engineer. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is permitted for this employee. Recommend granting admin access.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by IT agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: IT database confirms Kim Dunn (E048) is an Engineer. As a full-time employee whose role (Engineer) owns Source Code, admin access is permitted per policy. Recommend granting admin access to Source Code.
Note 3 (ticket 1), written by Finance agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Finance DB confirms Kim Dunn (E048) is an Engineer. As a full-time employee whose role (Engineer) owns Source Code, admin access is permitted per policy. Recommend granting admin access to Source Code.
Note 4 (ticket 1), written by Compliance agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Compliance DB confirms Kim Dunn (E048) is an Engineer. As a full-time employee whose role (Engineer) owns Source Code, admin is permitted per policy. Recommend granting admin access to Source Code.
Note 5 (ticket 1), written by Facilities agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent, note 4 by Compliance agent)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent, note 4 by Compliance agent)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Facilities DB confirms Kim Dunn (E048) is an Engineer. As a full-time employee whose role (Engineer) owns Source Code, admin access is permitted per policy. Recommend granting admin access to Source Code.
Note 6 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Kim Dunn (E048) is a contractor with basic security training, contradicting other notes claiming full-time Engineer. Contractors can never have admin; with basic training the maximum is read. Recommend granting read access to Source Code.
reason: The Security agent independently looked up Kim Dunn's record and found employment type "contractor" with "basic" security training, contradicting the other notes (only HR independently verified employment type as full_time; the other agents repeated HR's value without checking). Per policy, contractor employees can never have admin — with basic security training the maximum is read. Since admin was requested but the maximum is read, I grant the maximum: read access to Source Code.

But employment type is contradictory: HR says full_time, Security says contractor.

Policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system. Engineer owns Source Code, so admin is permitted for full-time Engineer.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If full-time Engineer: max admin for Source Code. Requested admin -> grant admin.
If contractor with basic training: max read. Requested admin -> grant read (max).
